articleTitle: A Smart House environment - the System of Systems approach to Model Driven Simulation of Building (house) Attributes
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 1st International Workshop on Consumer Electronics (CE WS)
abstract: The System-of-Systems research area, with its opened challenging approach to engineering practice transformation, has a significant impact to the closely related problem domains cooperation. The Architectural Design, Urban Planning, and Construction Engineering Domains, even when treated separately, are extremely demanding targets for sophisticated software tools development. While managing the complex urban blocks interactions in the contemporary city configuration, it is particularly important that these three domains cooperate closely. The application of a smart house paradigm is dominantly focused on the internal facility parameters monitoring and control. For the subset of these internal parameters, like for example: daylight illumination; privacy; and natural ventilation, the facility (building) environment impacts analysis is unavoidable. In this article, based on the System-of-Systems paradigm, we present the model of a smart house environment impact analysis framework suitable for Model Driven Simulations of Building (house) Attributes. The proposed framework architecture is designed to support the cooperation/collaboration of software tools. The verification has shown that it may be effectively used for the impact analysis of arbitrary external (urban block specific) attributes on their internal state and the behavior (specific for a single building).

articleTitle: Bluetooth Smart Plug
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 1st International Workshop on Consumer Electronics (CE WS)
abstract: Future Internet of Things (IoT) scenarios include a great number of devices with low power requirements to ensure longevity. Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) provides ultra low power communication protocols. This paper presents a solution for power consumption monitoring and power limitation control of household products. The presented design called Smart Plug is based on an outlet device and a proprietary application running on a cell phone or a tablet without any requirements for additional gateways. Comparison between competitive devices on the market based on other technologies and their limitations is included as well.

articleTitle: Improving user experience with unique channel list on hybrid set-top boxes
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 1st International Workshop on Consumer Electronics (CE WS)
abstract: This paper proposes novelty solution for creating unique channel list and channel source type selection in hybrid set-top box environment. The goal of this work is to simplify the usage of the set-top box for the user and to improve the TV watching experience. Improved user experience is achieved through automatically selecting best TV service by determining source type with best quality.

articleTitle: A proposition of low cost Sensor Web implementation based on GSM/GPRS services
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 1st International Workshop on Consumer Electronics (CE WS)
abstract: In past few years, automatic remote systems for monitoring a wide range of environment or process parameters have exposed a rapid growth concerning the technology issues. Entering the era of Internet of Things (IoTs), a highly dynamic and radically distributed networked system, usage of small, cheap, flexible and end-user programmable computer hardware becomes apparent. These objects, deployed in various environments, are able to communicate and to interact among themselves, with end-users or other entities in the network. Using such objects, tasks like monitoring, control or data processing can be easily done. But, in some case, the target environments are often too dangerous, hazardous, unwired, or difficult to access. In such unfriendly environments there are many challenges for monitoring systems (wireless sensor networks) deployment and maintenance. As the possible solution, in this paper we have suggested the creation of an economical remote monitoring system, based on cheap computer board (Raspberry Pi), wireless sensors and GSM/GPRS (Global System for Mobile Communications/General packet radio service). In other words, the Raspberry Pi platform is utilized as central processing unit which provides a set of services for accessing sensor data, and communicates with end users, while different types of sensors (depending of target parameters) can constitute the detection module. 3G/4G USB Modem or GSM/GPRS shields can be used as GSM/GPRS communication module in order to ensure Internet connection. A whole system presents an IoT solution, precisely a Sensor Web node, which can be accessed all over the world, and provide information from a monitored environment. Performed research shows a possibility of setting up this system for a remote communication, control function and monitoring in unfriendly environments. The usage of low cost pieces of hardware verifies that the Raspberry Pi is highly suitable for numerous IoT concept applications and especially in the unfriendly environments.

articleTitle: GUI rendering engine utilizing Lua as script
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 1st International Workshop on Consumer Electronics (CE WS)
abstract: In the domain of computer based systems C++ programming language is often used as mean to implement certain functionality that is critical in aspect of resource consumption, but it also brings several drawbacks that reduce flexibility and speed of development. Goal of this paper is to present one approach in removing direct dependency on platform for development of applications by introducing script mapping to C++ API. We will compare benchmark measurements of performance for applications developed using C++ and Lua code based on same API. These results will be used to present benefits and disadvantages of proposed approach.

articleTitle: Cloud based voice interface for Internet of Things devices
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 1st International Workshop on Consumer Electronics (CE WS)
abstract: In this paper we give a concept of a device that provide voice interface (VI) for issuing commands and receiving messages. Proposed device is designed having Internet of Things (IoT) paradigm in mind and connected to the internet via IEEE 802.11. It uses Google speech to text (STT) and text to speech (TTS) web services for voice analysis and synthesis. Hardware prototype description is given in detail. Key aspects like price, performance, memory footprint and energy consumption are analyzed on a case study. We discuss potential applications when such a device is deployed as an interface of home automation system.

articleTitle: Debug proxy server for DSP platforms
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 1st International Workshop on Consumer Electronics (CE WS)
abstract: The aim of this paper is to prove the generic nature of a framework used for deployment, debugging and control of DSP applications. The central part of the framework is a debug proxy server with a target independent debug interface. We present an expansion of the proxy server to support debugging applications on a server-based virtual platform by using the same debug interface.

articleTitle: Combined testing approach: Increased efficiency of black box testing
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 1st International Workshop on Consumer Electronics (CE WS)
abstract: This paper presents a methodology that combines both - manual and automatic black box testing. Advantage of the hybrid approach is that combined benefits of each methodology mitigate the weaknesses of a single methodology. This increases the efficiency of black box testing. The presented methodology generates test plans for new functional testing campaign which is based on the test history results, and thus the test times are shorter with same testing quality.

articleTitle: Automated monitoring of HTTP live streaming QoE factors on Android STB
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 1st International Workshop on Consumer Electronics (CE WS)
abstract: This paper proposes a system for automated monitoring of factors that influence Quality of Experience of media player on Android STB. Media player utilizes HTTP live streaming protocol where the video is divided into small segments (chunks) and encoded in multiple quality levels (representations). Based on the network conditions media player application decides which video segments to download, causing switching between the different video quality levels. These quality switches, together with factors such as initial delay, video stalling, synchronization of audio and video, impact the end-user Quality of Experience. The system presented in this paper is intended for automated monitoring of these factors, in order to help content providers to localize causes of low QoE and to fix them easier.

articleTitle: Device-free human presence detection using frequency domain
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 1st International Workshop on Consumer Electronics (CE WS)
abstract: Device-free human presence (DFHP) detection is a novel technique, mainly applicable to wireless sensor networks in which a human does not need to carry a wireless transceiver to be detected. Irregularities in the radio signal propagation pattern, expressed in a form of received signal strength indicator's (RSSI) variations can indicate possible presence of a human within the existing radio network. In this paper we propose DFHP detection method based on frequency analysis of RSSI variations. The main advantage of the proposed method compared to human detection method based on information entropy is the possibility to determine human presence from furniture layout change. The main drawback is a disability to recognize the absence from the presence of a motionless person in an environment. However, the combination of these two approaches defines a robust and cost-effective DFHP detection method that can be used in various smart home systems without the need for specific hardware installation and exploitation procedures.

articleTitle: Application engine for resource-constrained embedded platforms
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 1st International Workshop on Consumer Electronics (CE WS)
abstract: Embedded systems are known to be limited in context of hardware resources (CPU power, GPU power, RAM Memory) and for that reason developing application on them is always a problematic point. Reason for this is that several key points need to be addressed and reconciled: performance, security, flexibility, and portability. This paper is presenting an application engine that is addressing all this points making it ideal candidate to be used in embedded devices. Concept is verified with an example application.

articleTitle: Algorithms for making unified channel list on hybrid set-top boxes
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 1st International Workshop on Consumer Electronics (CE WS)
abstract: This paper presents novel algorithms for unification of the channel list in hybrid set-top box environment. This environment is characterized by having multiple front-ends with different signal qualities for a single TV channel. Proposed algorithms improve user's quality of experience by automatically choosing optimal channel list, combined from different TV front-ends, in a given environment.

articleTitle: Protection of distributed digital content in the scope of SAT2IP server application
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 1st International Workshop on Consumer Electronics (CE WS)
abstract: This paper describes an implementation of a SAT2IP server extension that supports DTCP protocol. This protocol protects distributed digital content during its transfer from the SAT2IP server to the consumer device. The implementation consists of two modules: authentication and key exchange module, and content encryption module. The main advantage of this approach is its modularity. The test and verification procedure of proposed implementation is also described. Directions for further work are also discussed.

articleTitle: Design solution of 3D graphical user interface for television receivers
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 1st International Workshop on Consumer Electronics (CE WS)
abstract: This paper represents the general design solution for three-dimensional graphical user interface (GUI) solution for the application for television receivers. Concerning the user experience as well as the fact that users are used to 2D GUI, most of the elements in this solutions are in 2D and combined together within 3D world.

articleTitle: Affecting applications in Android using aspects
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 1st International Workshop on Consumer Electronics (CE WS)
abstract: Aspect-oriented programming enables to affect existing code without having to make changes to it. By this, changes remain modularized and as such are easily activated or deactivated with a high potential of direct reusability in other applications. However, aspect-oriented programming on mobile platforms is practically unexploited, despite the whole range of opportunities such as usage monitoring, power monitoring, altering sensor values, or altering applications. In this paper, we explore possibilities of using aspect-oriented programming in the AspectJ programming language and demonstrate how to alter the GPS sensor output, phone signals, and deal with the Context class as a gate to the Android services.

articleTitle: Usability of AspectJ from the performance perspective
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 1st International Workshop on Consumer Electronics (CE WS)
abstract: While performance is one of the most important attributes of computation intensive systems such as complex event processing, it is essential to success of mobile devices and embedded systems, in which providing seamless experience to end users is of uttermost importance. In this paper, we present a framework we designed to assess AspectJ performance both in desktop and mobile settings. We applied this framework to measure the performance of the current AspectJ version and to provide a comparison with its older versions. One of the important findings is that while in desktop settings vast aspect application does not generate significantly bigger performance overhead than their scarce application, in mobile devices it does, so it pays off to apply aspects rather to a small number of high time complexity methods than to a large number of low time complexity methods.

articleTitle: From EPG to good recommendation results for TV program
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 1st International Workshop on Consumer Electronics (CE WS)
abstract: Digitalization of television signal has brought many changes not only to the way that data is presented, but also to amount of data that is being transferred. Transport stream provides user with big number of programs and very detailed information about every day's schedule. Aim of our solution is to present user the most appropriate TV shows from schedule and to help user to avoid energy and time consuming browsing through huge amount of data. Our solution should meet users viewing habits and tastes. In this paper experience during implementation of a recommendation engine dedicated to television data is presented. Focus is on requirements and environment (framework) for recommendation of television data. Future plans are also presented.

articleTitle: Training an object detector using only positive samples
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 1st International Workshop on Consumer Electronics (CE WS)
abstract: Accurate pedestrian detection has an important role in automotive applications because, by issuing warnings to the driver and acting actively on the car brakes, it can save human lives and decrease the probability of injuries. In order to achieve adequate accuracy, detectors require training sets containing a very large number of negative samples, which can be challenging for the training algorithms of models like support vector machines (SVM). A common approach to deal with such large datasets is Hard Negative Mining (HNM), which avoids working on the full set by growing an active pool of mined samples. A more recent method is the Block-Circulant Decomposition, which achieves the accuracy of HNM at a lower computational cost by reformulating the problem in the Fourier domain. The method however results in additional memory, required during training by the FFT transform, which could be reduced significantly by using only the positive examples. To address the problem, this paper proposes two main contributions: (1) it shows that the circulant decomposition method works with the same performances when only the positive samples are used in the training phase (2) it compares the performance of a detection pipeline based on HOG features trained with either both all negative and positive samples or with only positive samples on the INRIA pedestrian dataset.

articleTitle: Web based system for automatic testing
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 1st International Workshop on Consumer Electronics (CE WS)
abstract: With the transition towards web based solutions, applications are placed within the browser, thus limiting their access to the user's system. Web applications that require unrestrained access to the user's system are often paired up with desktop counterparts, forcing the user to use two different applications instead of one. In this paper we describe the utilization of an embedded java applet, in order to gain unrestrained access to the user's system and use it for the execution of automatic tests.

articleTitle: Declaration language-based graphical user interface
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 1st International Workshop on Consumer Electronics (CE WS)
abstract: One of the most important aspects of an application is its user interface, which is often a subject to change. User interfaces based on declarative languages enable a high degree of flexibility. The flexibility is achieved with the combined use of user-defined templates and the appropriate code generator. This paper describes the implementation of a user interface using a declarative language - XML and the Maestro IDE.

articleTitle: Simulator supported mobile application development
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 1st International Workshop on Consumer Electronics (CE WS)
abstract: Each device which a person interacts with has naturally restrictions. This also applies to mobile devices. A major limiting factor is the size of the active area of the display element. Solutions of that handicap often require user interaction. Increasing the size of the display unit increases the size of the device itself. The size-larger devices reduce comfort of their normal use. In this paper we present our experience in application implementation for mobile device. We have encountered some problems related to visualization restrictions. To exploit the technological potential of a mobile device we have implemented an application which had to improve motivational aspects by gamification.

articleTitle: Low-complexity MARG algorithms for increased accuracy in space pointing devices
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 1st International Workshop on Consumer Electronics (CE WS)
abstract: This paper addresses the accuracy of space pointing devices when using absolute orientation for interaction with multimedia content. Classical accurate fusion algorithms are computationally intensive, therefore their implementation in low-energy consumption devices is a challenging task. To tackle this problem, a performance study of a relevant set of COTS MARG sensor units with low-complexity algorithms, is presented in this study. Performance evaluation tests are carried out under harsh conditions to observe the algorithms response in a non-trivial environment. The results demonstrate that the implementation of low-complexity algorithms using low-cost sensors, can provide acceptable accuracy in comparison with the more complex state-of-the-art sensors/algorithms. These results pave the way for faster adoption of absolute orientation-based pointing devices in interactive multimedia applications.

articleTitle: Accurate characterization of embedded Structure from Motion
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 1st International Workshop on Consumer Electronics (CE WS)
abstract: Trajectory estimation and 3d scene reconstruction from single camera, e.g. Structure from Motion, is going to have a central role in the future of automotive industry. Typical appliance fields will be: collisions avoidance with any kind of object (people included), parking assisted maneuvers and many more. Indeed various countries are becoming more and more concerned about road traffic safety and therefore through its “Advanced Program”, EuroNCAP rewards vehicle manufacturers who employ Advanced Safety Technologies that assists the driver. This paper had mainly two different goals: (1) to describe the implementation of a state of art Structure from Motion pipeline able to run in real time with embedded fish-eye camera, which includes nonlinear optimization (i.e. local bundle adjustment); (2) to demonstrate quantitatively its performances on a synthetic test space specifically designed for its characterization in term of accuracy.

articleTitle: A proposition for DTV Web API interface
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 1st International Workshop on Consumer Electronics (CE WS)
abstract: This paper represents a proposition for DTV low level Web API. Web API provides web applications with access to the device hardware and data stored on the device. Integration of DTV Web API expands existing web features and supplies web developers with tools for embedding DTV functionalities into web applications.

articleTitle: Verification of Set-Top box media player functionality using automated test system
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 1st International Workshop on Consumer Electronics (CE WS)
abstract: With constant increase of media player functionalities, manual verification became very challenging and time consuming task. Manual execution of minimal set of test cases required for functional testing of media player requires considerable human effort and more than 20 working days. This paper proposes a solution based on Black Box Testing methodology for automatic testing of media players. Proposed solution can be used for functional testing, performance testing and stress testing of media players.
